---
title: "6. OpenFold (Optional)"
---

OpenFold ([paper](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2022.11.20.517210v1), [code](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold)) is a faithful, trainable PyTorch reproduction of DeepMind's AlphaFold2. It achieves performance comparable to AlphaFold2 and provides a fully open-source implementation for protein structure prediction.

## Why Use OpenFold?

- **Full transparency**: Open-source model architecture and training code
- **Trainable**: Can be fine-tuned or retrained on custom data
- **Research-friendly**: Ideal for understanding how structure prediction works
- **MSA-based accuracy**: Uses evolutionary information for high-accuracy predictions

**Related Tools**: For faster predictions without MSAs, see [ESMFold](5-esmfold.qmd). For a more user-friendly MSA-based option, see [LocalColabFold](2-localcolabfold.qmd).

## Recorded course pin
The commands below use OpenFold commit `be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d` (reviewed 2026-08-30). OpenFold's database and compiler requirements vary substantially by cluster; run the preflight and read the fallback route in [Reproducible Setup & Compute Fallbacks](reproducibility.qmd) before downloading databases.
:::

## Resource Requirements

| Resource | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|----------|---------|-------------|-------|
| GPU RAM | 16 GB | 40+ GB | A100 for large proteins |
| CPU RAM | 32 GB | 64+ GB | MSA generation is memory-intensive |
| Disk Space | 500 GB | 2+ TB | Sequence databases are large |
| CUDA | 11.3+ | 12.4 | The pinned upstream environment resolves PyTorch CUDA 12.4 |

**Note**: OpenFold requires significant disk space for sequence databases if generating MSAs locally. Check if your HPC already has AlphaFold/OpenFold databases installed.

## Preparation

[Mark as complete]{.task module-id="openfold-prep"}

**Prerequisites**:

- Completed [HPC Setup](1-hpc-setup.qmd) guide
- Conda/Mamba installed
- `nvcc` available for CUDA compilation
- Significant disk space (or access to shared databases)

**Check for existing databases**:
```bash
# Ask your HPC admins or check common locations
ls /shared/databases/alphafold/
ls /shared/databases/openfold/
```

Many HPCs have pre-installed AlphaFold databases that OpenFold can use.

## Installation

[Mark as complete]{.task module-id="openfold-install"}

**Important**: OpenFold installation can be complex. The official documentation at [openfold.readthedocs.io](https://openfold.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) has the most current instructions.

1. Clone the repository:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold.git
cd openfold
git checkout --detach be2ec1841f16c966c65ae0e7599ebbadc725757d
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

2. Create the conda environment:
```bash
mamba env create -f environment.yml
mamba activate openfold_venv
```

**Expected time**: 10-20 minutes for environment creation.

3. Install OpenFold:
```bash
pip install -e .
```

4. Download model weights:
```bash
bash scripts/download_openfold_params.sh openfold/resources
```

**Expected download**: ~1-2 GB of model weights.

5. (Optional) Download sequence databases for MSA generation:
```bash
# This downloads ~2TB of data - skip if using HPC shared databases
bash scripts/download_alphafold_dbs.sh /path/to/database/directory
```

## Testing the Installation

[Mark as complete]{.task module-id="openfold-test"}

Create `input_fastas/test_protein.fasta` (create the directory first with `mkdir -p input_fastas`). Keep one sequence per file and use unique FASTA headers:
```
>test_protein
MKTVRQERLKSIVRILERSKEPVSGAQLAEELSVSRQVIVQDIAYLRSLGYNIVATPRGYVLAGG
```

The pinned CLI takes a **directory of FASTA files**, then a **directory of template mmCIF files**. The second argument is not the sequence database root. For a short test, obtain precomputed alignments for this exact sequence from your instructor or generate them using the local-database example below. Alignment subdirectories must match FASTA header identifiers (for this example, `test_protein`).

Run a prediction using those precomputed MSAs:

```bash
python run_pretrained_openfold.py \
    input_fastas/ \
    /path/to/pdb_mmcif/mmcif_files \
    --use_precomputed_alignments /path/to/precomputed_alignments \
    --output_dir predictions/ \
    --config_preset model_1_ptm \
    --model_device cuda:0
```

**Note**: Precomputed alignments avoid sequence database searches; template mmCIF files are still required. An arbitrary empty alignment directory is not an equivalent test.

**Success indicators**:

- Command completes without errors
- `predictions/` directory contains PDB files
- Output includes confidence metrics (pLDDT, pTM)

**Expected runtime**: 5-30 minutes depending on MSA availability and protein size.

## HPC Job Script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=openfold
#SBATCH --partition=gpu
#SBATCH --gpus=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=64G
#SBATCH --time=08:00:00
#SBATCH --output=%x_%j.out

module load cuda/12.4

# source ~/.bashrc # Source shell profile if needed
mamba activate openfold_venv

cd /path/to/openfold

# Reuse alignments prepared on a CPU node before allocating the GPU.
FASTA_DIR=/path/to/input_fastas
TEMPLATE_MMCIF_DIR=/shared/databases/alphafold/pdb_mmcif/mmcif_files
ALIGNMENT_DIR=/path/to/precomputed_alignments

python run_pretrained_openfold.py \
    "$FASTA_DIR" \
    "$TEMPLATE_MMCIF_DIR" \
    --use_precomputed_alignments "$ALIGNMENT_DIR" \
    --output_dir predictions/ \
    --config_preset model_1_ptm \
    --model_device cuda:0
```

## Usage Examples

**Basic prediction with local databases**:

Set these paths to the database release installed by your administrator. The filenames below are examples; all database prefixes and sequence files must exist. Keep the FASTA sequences, database release, and template settings with the run record so cached alignments are reused only for compatible inputs.

```bash
FASTA_DIR=/path/to/input_fastas
TEMPLATE_MMCIF_DIR=/shared/databases/alphafold/pdb_mmcif/mmcif_files
DATABASE_DIR=/shared/databases/alphafold
DATABASE_ARGS=(
    --uniref90_database_path "$DATABASE_DIR/uniref90/uniref90.fasta"
    --mgnify_database_path "$DATABASE_DIR/mgnify/mgy_clusters_2022_05.fa"
    --bfd_database_path "$DATABASE_DIR/bfd/bfd_metaclust_clu_complete_id30_c90_final_seq.sorted_opt"
    --uniref30_database_path "$DATABASE_DIR/uniref30/UniRef30_2021_03"
    --pdb70_database_path "$DATABASE_DIR/pdb70/pdb70"
)

python run_pretrained_openfold.py \
    "$FASTA_DIR" "$TEMPLATE_MMCIF_DIR" \
    "${DATABASE_ARGS[@]}" \
    --cpus 8 \
    --output_dir output_model_1_ptm/ \
    --config_preset model_1_ptm \
    --model_device cuda:0
```

This first prediction creates `output_model_1_ptm/alignments/`, with one subdirectory per FASTA header. Complete and verify it before starting other presets; do not let concurrent jobs write the same alignment cache.

**Using precomputed MSAs** (no sequence database searches):

```bash
python run_pretrained_openfold.py \
    "$FASTA_DIR" "$TEMPLATE_MMCIF_DIR" \
    --use_precomputed_alignments /path/to/precomputed_alignments \
    --output_dir output/ \
    --config_preset model_1_ptm \
    --model_device cuda:0
```

**Multiple model presets** (ensemble):

After the first `model_1_ptm` prediction above succeeds, run the remaining two presets against its completed alignments. The cache is shared, but each preset has its own prediction directory. This performs the expensive alignment searches once across the three-model ensemble.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
ALIGNMENT_DIR="$PWD/output_model_1_ptm/alignments"
test -d "$ALIGNMENT_DIR"
for preset in model_2_ptm model_3_ptm; do
    python run_pretrained_openfold.py \
        "$FASTA_DIR" "$TEMPLATE_MMCIF_DIR" \
        --use_precomputed_alignments "$ALIGNMENT_DIR" \
        --config_preset "$preset" \
        --output_dir "output_${preset}/" \
        --model_device cuda:0
done
```

Regenerate alignments in a new directory when sequences, identifiers, database releases, or alignment/template settings change. An existing directory alone does not prove the previous job completed successfully.

## Model Presets

| Preset | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `model_1_ptm` | Standard model with pTM head |
| `model_2_ptm` | Alternative model with pTM |
| `model_3_ptm` | Third model variant |
| `model_1_multimer_v3` | For protein complexes |

## Understanding the Output

Output directory structure:
```
predictions/
├── test_protein_model_1_ptm_unrelaxed.pdb    # Predicted structure
├── test_protein_model_1_ptm_confidences.json # Confidence scores
└── test_protein_model_1_ptm_timings.json     # Runtime statistics
```

**Confidence metrics**:

- **pLDDT**: Per-residue confidence (0-100, higher is better)
- **pTM**: Predicted TM-score (0-1, >0.8 is confident)
- **PAE**: Predicted Aligned Error matrix

## Database Requirements

If generating MSAs locally, OpenFold needs these databases:

| Database | Size | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| BFD | ~1.7 TB | Sequence alignments |
| MGnify | ~120 GB | Metagenomic sequences |
| UniRef90 | ~100 GB | Sequence clustering |
| UniRef30 | ~200 GB | HHblits templates |
| PDB70 | ~60 GB | Structure templates |

**Total**: ~2+ TB

**Check HPC shared databases first** - most research HPCs have these pre-installed.

## Troubleshooting

::: {.callout-warning}
## Common Issues


**Compilation errors during install**:
```bash
# Ensure CUDA toolkit is loaded
module load cuda/12.4
nvcc --version

# Clean and retry
pip uninstall openfold
pip install -e .
```

**"Database not found" errors**:

- Verify database paths exist
- Check HPC documentation for shared database locations
- Contact HPC admins about AlphaFold database availability

**Out of memory**:

- Request more GPU memory
- Reduce `--max_recycling_iters`
- Use gradient checkpointing for training

**Slow MSA generation**:

- MSA generation is CPU-bound and can take hours
- Use pre-computed MSAs when possible
- Consider using ColabFold's MMseqs2 server instead

**Model weights not found**:
```bash
# Re-download weights
bash scripts/download_openfold_params.sh openfold/resources

# Verify files exist
ls openfold/resources/*.pt
```
:::

## For Researchers: Training

OpenFold can be retrained or fine-tuned:

```bash
python train_openfold.py \
    /path/to/training/data \
    /path/to/template_mmcif \
    /path/to/output \
    --config_preset initial_training
```

See the [training documentation](https://openfold.readthedocs.io/en/stable/Training_OpenFold.html) for details.
